vtIzMaLkCaM.summary: Larry McEnerney of the University of Chicago Writing Program gives a graduate-student session on writing effectively. His core idea is that readers care about value to them, not the writer's thinking process.
vtIzMaLkCaM.why: HN users repeatedly say it changed how they think about writing, calling it a masterclass useful far beyond academia.

vK1DazRK_a0.summary: Rafal Dittwald's Clojure/north talk shows how to move from writing Java-style code in Clojure to thinking in data-driven, functional terms. He walks through a JavaScript example, refactoring imperative code step by step into a functional core.
vK1DazRK_a0.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as a fantastic demonstration of procedural, OOP and FP approaches to the same problem, and of functional core and imperative shell.

vpTHi7O66pI.summary: Allan Savory's TED talk arguing that desertification of grasslands can be reversed with holistic managed grazing, which he says would also help reverse climate change. TED notes that other scientists have challenged his claims.
vpTHi7O66pI.why: HN commenters bring it up in climate and food threads as a hopeful, if contested, idea about grazing and soil carbon.

vsMydMDi3rI.summary: Frank Abagnale, the real subject of Catch Me If You Can, speaks at Google about his life as a con man turned FBI fraud and cybersecurity expert, including advice on fraud, breaches and credit cards.
vsMydMDi3rI.why: Praised as a charismatic, engaging talk with practical security lessons, like why credit cards protect you better than debit cards.

vTMF6xEiAaY.summary: A People Make Games follow-up investigation into Roblox, built on stories from players and creators after the channel's first video. It covers the platform's treatment of young developers and its moderation.
vTMF6xEiAaY.why: Cited heavily in Roblox threads as a damning investigation into child labor, exploitation, and weak moderation, and suggested viewing for parents.

vq2nnJ4g6N0.summary: Martin Gorner's Devoxx talk introduces deep learning with TensorFlow, walking through neural networks for MNIST, how to choose an architecture and how to diagnose networks that fail to train.
vq2nnJ4g6N0.why: Repeatedly called an excellent, practical introduction that covers a lot in two hours and explains issues academic textbooks skip.

v1WiCGq-PcY.summary: A one-minute clip of Bryan Cranston at an Academy new-member reception, advising actors to approach auditions without desperation and focus on solving the problem rather than landing the job.
v1WiCGq-PcY.why: HN applies it to job interviews and confidence, recommending the mindset of not interviewing from a place of desperation.

vgT4Y30DkaA.summary: The original trailer for Threads, the 1984 British TV film depicting the aftermath of a nuclear attack on Sheffield. The trailer hints at the film's bleak tone.
vgT4Y30DkaA.why: HN commenters use it to point people to Threads, which they call the most harrowing depiction of nuclear war and say should be mandatory viewing.

vvZA9n3e5pc.summary: Bryan Cantrill of Oxide Computer Company gives a Stanford EE380 talk on rethinking the server. He argues that hyperscaler-style rack-scale machines with open firmware, RISC-V and Rust should be available to everyone, not just the giants.
vvZA9n3e5pc.why: HN points to it as the founders' own explanation of what Oxide is building and why, a frequent link whenever Oxide comes up.

vzfy4EKwG_Y.summary: Richard Feldman explains how pure functional languages can match or beat imperative ones on performance. Compilers can turn immutable code into in-place mutation, avoiding naive copying. The talk draws on his work on the Roc language.
vzfy4EKwG_Y.why: Recommended as the clearest explanation of why immutable data need not be slow, and as the introduction to Roc.

vYA0f6R5KAI.summary: SpaceX engineers present at NVIDIA's GPU Technology Conference on a multi-physics code that simulates the full-scale Raptor methane engine. It covers GPU-based turbulent combustion modeling with adaptive grids and wavelet compression.
vYA0f6R5KAI.why: HN points to it as evidence of SpaceX's serious simulation capability and as a showcase of GPU compute for CFD.

vwCdKU9uYnE.summary: A Computer History Museum oral history with Avie Tevanian covering his math talent, work on the Mach microkernel at CMU, joining NeXT, leading NEXTSTEP development and the 1996 Apple acquisition.
vwCdKU9uYnE.why: Recommended as a long, rich first-hand account of Mach, NeXT and Apple history and of working for Steve Jobs.

v3pYRn5j7oI.summary: A clip from the 1983 BBC series Fun to Imagine in which Richard Feynman explains heat as the jiggling of atoms and how we perceive it as hot and cold.
v3pYRn5j7oI.why: Recommended as a short, joyful example of Feynman's accessible way of explaining physics, which a transcript cannot capture.

v3y8AIEX_dU.summary: Kurzgesagt explains stellar engines such as the Shkadov thruster and Caplan thruster, which could move the Sun and solar system across the galaxy over millions of years to avoid hazards and reach new regions.
v3y8AIEX_dU.why: HN returns to it whenever moving the solar system, Kardashev civilizations or generation ships come up, with some calling it their favorite Kurzgesagt video.

v7Mt0GYHU9A.summary: Aaron Hsu discusses design patterns and anti-patterns in APL and why the language is productive despite its write-only reputation. He argues that idioms matter more than libraries in array languages.
v7Mt0GYHU9A.why: HN recommends it as a terrific talk on APL readability and on the idea of idioms over libraries.

vuIlsN32WaE.summary: Ruben Meerman presents a TEDx talk on the stoichiometry of weight loss, showing with lab demonstrations where fat goes when it is lost. He argues that most of it is exhaled as carbon dioxide.
vuIlsN32WaE.why: HN regularly shares it in weight loss threads as a clear, precise explanation of the physics of weight loss.

v0YEaeIClKY.summary: A short 3Blue1Brown video explaining Euler's formula e^(i*pi) = -1 through dynamics, treating velocity as the thing that moves a point to a new position. It builds geometric intuition for why an exponent with i produces rotation.
v0YEaeIClKY.why: HN commenters point to it as a quick, visual way to understand Euler's identity.

vJjKwSF9gT8.summary: Engineering Explained examines Toyota's hydrogen-burning V8 engine built with Yamaha and explains the practical problems of hydrogen combustion vehicles. It covers efficiency, storage and distribution issues.
vJjKwSF9gT8.why: HN uses it as the go-to explanation of why hydrogen internal combustion engines do not make sense.

vuEQixrBKCc.summary: A George Carlin stand-up bit on euphemisms, tracing how language gets softened, such as shell shock becoming PTSD, until it loses its emotional force.
vuEQixrBKCc.why: HN commenters reach for it whenever a thread involves corporate or political euphemism, using it mostly as a reference.

v6jhjjVy5Ls.summary: Coffeezilla's investigation into the Counter-Strike 2 skin gambling ecosystem, covering casino sites, influencers and esports teams that profit from it. It is part of a multi-part series on Valve's skin economy and its effects on young players.
v6jhjjVy5Ls.why: HN commenters recommend it as an investigative look at CS skin gambling and the exploitation of minors.

vGAqYNFQdZ4.summary: A 1945 US Army educational film that dramatizes how demagogues use prejudice and scapegoating to divide people. It opens with fake wrestling matches and crooked gambling games to show how con artists work, then applies the lesson to racial and religious bigotry.
vGAqYNFQdZ4.why: HN commenters bring it up in political threads as a classic warning about divisive agitators and fascism, and suggest it be remade for each generation.

v_UyVmITiYQ.summary: The Google I/O 2009 keynote introducing Google Wave, a real-time collaborative communication and document platform. It includes a long live demo and the developer preview announcement.
v_UyVmITiYQ.why: HN returns to it as the original Wave pitch, both for its wow factor and as a case study in a hyped product that was later shut down.

vmgxtcbc4iU.summary: A Sam Harris podcast episode from June 2020 on the protests and unrest after George Floyd's death, discussing racism and police violence in America in light of the available data.
vmgxtcbc4iU.why: HN commenters recommend it as a data-oriented discussion of race and police shootings.

vu-h5y6tK34.summary: Urban Bruhin, LibrePCB's main author, introduces the open-source EDA tool at FOSDEM 2018. He explains why he started it and how its library concepts differ from KiCAD.
vu-h5y6tK34.why: Linked by the author and others in LibrePCB threads as the best explanation of its design rationale.

v3pK0dccQ38.summary: Ivor Cummins gives an 82-minute presentation on the history and science of vitamin D and human health. He draws on expert interviews to argue that sun exposure and vitamin D status are linked to many chronic diseases.
v3pK0dccQ38.why: HN commenters point to it in vitamin D threads as a thorough walkthrough of why deficiency may matter.

vJG698U2Mvo.summary: The original invisible gorilla awareness test by Daniel Simons and Christopher Chabris, in which viewers count basketball passes and often miss a gorilla crossing the scene. It demonstrates inattentional blindness.
vJG698U2Mvo.why: HN uses it constantly as the classic demonstration that attention is selective, in threads on driving, motorcycles, AI and perception.

vNaEBbFbvcY.summary: A PBS Space Time episode asking what black holes really are and whether events can happen inside them. It covers event horizons, time dilation and common misconceptions about black holes.
vNaEBbFbvcY.why: HN commenters recommend it as an accessible but deep explanation of black holes that corrects popular misconceptions.

vYLEuQrvND0.summary: Ross Scott's Game Dungeon episode critiques Deus Ex: Human Revolution, looking at its design, politics and visual style. It is part of his series of opinionated game reviews.
vYLEuQrvND0.why: HN commenters recommend it as a witty critique of the game, and cite it in discussions of the yellow filter in games.

vyenmLqJQjs.summary: Greg Kroah-Hartman's Git Merge 2016 talk on how the Linux kernel is developed, how fast it moves, and how git and email workflows keep it manageable. He is the stable kernel maintainer.
vyenmLqJQjs.why: HN points to it as an authoritative overview of the kernel's email-and-git workflow and its development rate.

v7AYyUqrMuQ.summary: VICE News reporter Isobel Yeung goes undercover as a tourist in Xinjiang, documenting heavy surveillance, policing and internment of Uighurs. It also covers children taken into state-run institutions.
v7AYyUqrMuQ.why: HN cites it as first-hand, independent reporting on Xinjiang that does not rely on state-sanctioned access.

vHWiDx_l4V0.summary: A Zig SHOWTIME talk by Benjamin Feng on what a memory allocator is, followed by an interview. It covers allocation strategies and different allocator types in Zig.
vHWiDx_l4V0.why: Recommended as a quick, clear overview of allocators and arenas that also shows how Zig approaches allocation.

vKA4w2O61Xo.summary: A Veritasium video that runs the 2-4-8 rule-guessing puzzle on people to show how they test only examples that confirm their hypothesis. It uses this to illustrate confirmation bias and falsification.
vKA4w2O61Xo.why: Recommended as a clear demonstration of confirmation bias and the value of trying to break your own hypothesis.

vOvQCPLkPt4.summary: A Microsoft Research demo from TechFest 2012 of a lab touch system that lets viewers feel the effect of different input latencies, down to about 1 ms. It shows how much more responsive dragging feels compared with typical 100 ms touch delay.
vOvQCPLkPt4.why: HN commenters cite it whenever input latency comes up, as the demonstration that people can perceive touch delay down to 1 ms.

vWkgEddb4-A.summary: David Sanders gives the first part of a two-part introduction to the Julia programming language at SciPy 2014. It walks through the language's basics and its appeal for scientific computing.
vWkgEddb4-A.why: HN commenters point newcomers to it as a solid starting point for getting to know Julia.

vaCVh2SAZY4.summary: Shawn Hymel of DigiKey introduces KiCad and explains how printed circuit boards are manufactured. It is the first part of a beginner series that builds a 555 badge project.
vaCVh2SAZY4.why: Recommended as a friendly starting point for people who want to learn PCB design with free tools.

vs41JrnGaxc.summary: Psychologist Jonathan Haidt presents his moral foundations research in a TED talk. He argues that liberals and conservatives weigh a different set of moral values, which helps explain political divides.
vs41JrnGaxc.why: HN recommends it as an accessible way to understand why people across the political spectrum disagree and to better understand opposing views.

vtWp45Eewtw.summary: Periodic Videos visits a fluorine expert to show how reactive the element is in action. It also includes a discussion of fluoride and tooth enamel.
vtWp45Eewtw.why: Recommended in fluoride and fluorine threads as a short, fun demonstration of how nasty fluorine is.

vDwzmJpI4io.summary: Sal Khan interviews Elon Musk in a 2013 Khan Academy entrepreneurship series. Musk discusses PayPal, rocket efficiency and reusability, and how he approaches education and learning.
vDwzmJpI4io.why: HN cites it as a source for specific Musk anecdotes and as an immensely interesting full conversation.

vN4U5FqrOdQ.summary: The full January 2007 Macworld keynote where Steve Jobs unveils the first iPhone. It covers the touch interface, multitouch gestures, the browser, maps and the pitch as an iPod, phone and internet communicator.
vN4U5FqrOdQ.why: HN points to it as a landmark product presentation and as primary-source evidence of what the original iPhone was meant to do and how people reacted.

vVX-PrBRtTY.summary: A short clip from The West Wing in which characters argue for the Gall-Peters map projection over Mercator. It dramatizes how standard maps distort the relative size of countries.
vVX-PrBRtTY.why: It is the go-to link in any HN thread on map projections, usually posted as the obligatory West Wing reference.

vc4yL3YTwWk.summary: MegaLag investigates PayPal's Honey browser extension, showing how it swaps affiliate attribution and was promoted by large YouTube influencers. It includes technical demonstrations of the affiliate tag replacement in browser dev tools.
vc4yL3YTwWk.why: HN treats it as top-tier investigative journalism on YouTube and the video that triggered lawsuits against Honey.

vq2BxAJZ4Tc.summary: The first video in a series on extremely large numbers, introducing the topic with examples. Later parts go deep into the fast-growing hierarchy.
vq2BxAJZ4Tc.why: Recommended in large-number threads as going further than other popular videos on Graham's number and ordinals.

v19cu2hj2Ms.summary: Clickspring makes the pin-and-slot epicyclic gearing of the Antikythera Mechanism, the module modelling the Moon's variable motion in the Greek theory, by hand.
v19cu2hj2Ms.why: Recommended as a beautiful explanation of how the mechanism models the Moon's uneven motion.

v68zYyaEmEA.summary: 3Blue1Brown uses Wordle as an excuse to teach information theory and entropy, building a solver that picks guesses by expected information and incorporating word frequencies.
v68zYyaEmEA.why: HN recommends it as the go-to explanation of optimal Wordle openers like CRANE and a friendly introduction to information theory, also relevant to Mastermind.

v8IQ-X2HkGE.summary: John A. De Goes's Scalapeno keynote argues that Scala's popularity is declining because of compile times, complexity and compatibility problems. He proposes a path for Scala to survive, including a simplified functional subset.
v8IQ-X2HkGE.why: Cited in Scala and language-marketing discussions for its accurate account of Scala's pain points and its argument that a language's pitch must address a real developer pain.

vAHXK2wut_I.summary: A speedrunner-made explanation of the Super Mario World credits warp, an arbitrary code execution glitch that jumps the game straight to the ending. It simplifies the underlying assembly and memory behavior with animations so non-experts can follow.
vAHXK2wut_I.why: HN people cite it as the clearest explanation of how the credits warp exploit works.

vBiIDwBOqQA.summary: Biochemist Nick Lane gives a Royal Institution lecture arguing that the Krebs cycle is central to what makes cells alive, not just genetic information. He draws on the themes of his book Transformer to link metabolism to the origin of life, death, and aging.
vBiIDwBOqQA.why: HN commenters point to Nick Lane as an excellent science communicator whose talks on mitochondria and the chemistry of life are worth watching.

vI5pbDFDZyI.summary: A short Not Just Bikes video on the 1960s plans (Plan Jokinen) to cut highways through Amsterdam to accommodate cars. It shows how radically different the city would look had they succeeded.
vI5pbDFDZyI.why: HN commenters cite it as a concise illustration of how the Netherlands narrowly avoided car-centric planning and then built its bike culture.

vPnehDhGa14.summary: TheRasteri installs MS-DOS and Windows 1.0, then upgrades in place through nearly every Windows version up to Windows 7, checking which programs survive. Even Doom from 1993 still runs at the end.
vPnehDhGa14.why: HN cites it as evidence of Microsoft's backward compatibility and of upgrade engineering done well.

vQpUV--2Jao.summary: A Wendover Productions video on how dollar store chains expanded across America and why they displace grocery stores in small towns. It covers their business model and supplier leverage.
vQpUV--2Jao.why: Offered as a good explanation of the business of dollar stores and how they affect local grocers.

vT1JzLTH4G4.summary: The first lecture of Stanford's CS231n course on convolutional neural networks for visual recognition. It surveys the history and key challenges of computer vision, from the Cambrian explosion and Hubel and Wiesel to ImageNet.
vT1JzLTH4G4.why: HN recommends the CS231n lectures as a solid, applied deep learning course for self-study.

vTbILK0fxDY.summary: PolyMatter's first part of a series on China's demographic collapse, covering the effects of the one-child policy, shrinking workforce and economic consequences.
vTbILK0fxDY.why: Offered as a starter for people wanting to understand China's demographic crisis and how it threatens economic growth.

vU1-uiUlHTo.summary: Benn Jordan concludes his Flock trilogy, filmed on a publicly deployed Flock Safety camera, covering a leak of camera feeds reported by 404 Media. He shows the cameras' capabilities, including panning to track people.
vU1-uiUlHTo.why: HN points to it as in-depth independent coverage of Flock license-plate cameras and their security and surveillance problems.

vXBfwgwT1nQ.summary: Mark Rober builds a machine that plays the Cyclone arcade game with perfect timing and discovers the game is rigged so that perfect play still loses. The video explains the physics and electronics tricks behind carnival-style skill games.
vXBfwgwT1nQ.why: Cited in threads on rigged arcade machines and gambling-like games as the clearest demonstration that skill games can be tuned to be unwinnable.

vXjVFPosQHw.summary: Nicholas Zakas of Yahoo discusses architecture for large, modular JavaScript web applications. He lays out the theory behind building front ends that scale in complexity.
vXjVFPosQHw.why: Recommended as a framework-agnostic, common-sense guide to structuring large front-end applications.

vZ_a21fPkYM.summary: A BBC Four documentary following Alan Bond and Reaction Engines as they pursue the Skylon spaceplane and its SABRE engine. It covers the history from HOTOL and the heat-exchanger breakthrough.
vZ_a21fPkYM.why: Linked in Reaction Engines threads as the story behind the engine, though one commenter is skeptical of the company's funding record.

viJt_DXTfwA.summary: Computerphile interviews AI safety researcher Rob Miles about ChatGPT: how it was trained with human feedback, why it tends to produce confident nonsense, and where it may or may not be dangerous.
viJt_DXTfwA.why: HN commenters send it to people confused about ChatGPT's quirks, explaining how human-feedback training makes it a pleasing yes-man that bullshits.

vkYEYjintqU.summary: A short Harvard animation narrated by Professor Rob Lue introducing mitochondria as the cell's powerhouses and how cells turn food and oxygen into energy.
vkYEYjintqU.why: Recommended as a beautiful, accessible animation of cellular energy production.

vmwnhZmEZjc.summary: David Mazieres presents the Stellar Consensus Protocol at Google, introducing federated Byzantine agreement. The model lets participants choose whom to trust rather than assuming fixed membership.
vmwnhZmEZjc.why: Recommended as the protocol designer's own detailed explanation of SCP.

vt-zXEsJ61U.summary: Andreas Antonopoulos answers a question about how to secure your Bitcoin. He covers holding your own keys, backing up the 12 to 24 word seed phrase, and the tradeoffs of custodial accounts, phone wallets and hardware wallets.
vt-zXEsJ61U.why: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of self-custody and of why to move coins off exchanges.

vxopfjXkArM.summary: An Adam Ruins Everything segment claiming that jaywalking became a crime through campaigns by the auto industry. It is a short, comedic history of how streets were reclaimed for cars.
vxopfjXkArM.why: HN uses it as shorthand for the argument that car dominance was manufactured by deliberate propaganda.

v3XcQtoja_Y.summary: UploadVR covers a Facebook Reality Labs prototype that tracks facial expressions using cameras mounted in a VR headset. The updated version captures subtle micro-expressions for realistic avatars.
v3XcQtoja_Y.why: Pointed to in metaverse and VR threads as proof that realtime photorealistic face tracking from headset cameras is coming.

vtOA1vuoDgQ.summary: Seymour Cray's only surviving recorded talk, introducing the Cray-1 supercomputer in 1976. He describes the machine's design, including its vector architecture and cooling through the frame.
vtOA1vuoDgQ.why: Cited as a rare first-hand account from Cray, loved for details like the aluminum machining invented to carry Freon through the frame.

v0gjI__RyCY.summary: Dwarkesh Patel interviews Google's Jeff Dean and Noam Shazeer about 25 years at the company, from PageRank and MapReduce to the Transformer, mixture of experts and Gemini. They also discuss where AI is heading.
v0gjI__RyCY.why: HN cites it for insight into Google researchers' views on AI progress and publishing, though one commenter finds the interview weak.

v2Q_zHG3vqg.summary: A 2015 GDC talk by Bungie's Barry Genova on how Destiny's engine was restructured into a job graph with limited thread pre-emption. It is aimed at programmers of demanding game engines.
v2Q_zHG3vqg.why: HN points to it as a real-world example of game engine multithreading and of safety annotations in C.

v2RJQELoM6Y.summary: Martin Kleppmann's Kafka Summit 2018 keynote asks whether Kafka can be considered a database. He covers event logs and related data-systems ideas.
v2RJQELoM6Y.why: HN posts it in Kafka-as-database debates and as an introduction to event logs and CQRS.

v4Wy7gRGgeA.summary: A fan-made music video for Jonathan Coulton's song 'Code Monkey', about the life of a programmer, using World of Warcraft footage. It was made by Mike Spiff Booth.
v4Wy7gRGgeA.why: Mostly brought up as a joke or nostalgic reference when the term 'code monkey' comes up.

v8sl8gj9UnA.summary: Allan Jude of Klara presents work on making ZFS scale on fast NVMe storage, covering fixes to the TaskQueue interface and removal of bottlenecks. The talk was given at EuroBSDcon 2022 and describes raising write throughput from about 3 to over 7 GB/sec.
v8sl8gj9UnA.why: Cited in ZFS and filesystem threads as the go-to source on ZFS limits and tuning for NVMe.

v9EKV2nSU8w.summary: Writer and artist James Bridle shows how strange and disturbing children's videos on YouTube, from surprise eggs to algorithmic mashups, are produced for ad revenue. He argues they reveal problems in a data-driven internet.
v9EKV2nSU8w.why: Cited to explain how YouTube's algorithms produce appalling content aimed at children, and as a reason to keep kids off the platform.

vElZc6zSIXM.summary: Chandler Carruth's CppCon 2016 talk on designing hybrid data structures for performance. He covers cache locality, working-set size and allocation overhead, and why standard C++ containers fall short.
vElZc6zSIXM.why: Cited as the source for criticism of std::deque and move-constructor pitfalls, and as motivation to write custom data structures.

vJYaXy5mmA8.summary: A short Australian dystopian film in which a man returns home to find citizens fining each other for infractions via a government app, with cameras everywhere.
vJYaXy5mmA8.why: HN cites it as a vivid illustration of where automated enforcement, digital ID and crowd-sourced policing could lead.

vKmQW_Nkfk8.summary: Steve Yegge's OSCON Data 2011 talk imagines what you could do with Google-scale storage and compute a decade later. He argues smart people should work on hard problems such as biology rather than cat pictures, and the talk ends with a moment many took as him quitting Google.
vKmQW_Nkfk8.why: Cited for its critique of talent wasted on social media and for the data-mining-for-biology argument, plus the around-14-minute quitting moment.

vSSkDos2hzo.summary: Kurzgesagt explains why exercise alone does little for weight loss, since the body compensates by adjusting its total energy expenditure. It argues exercise is still very valuable for health.
vSSkDos2hzo.why: HN uses it as a sourced, accessible summary in weight-loss and GLP-1 threads.

vV7YgnPUxcU.summary: Ross Douthat interviews Peter Thiel about technological stagnation, AI, longevity, space travel and politics. Thiel also lays out his framing of the Antichrist as a risk of civilizational stagnation.
vV7YgnPUxcU.why: Commenters cite it as the primary source for Thiel's Antichrist argument whenever his views come up.

vVgc8ksstyg.summary: A short clip of the Harwell Dekatron/WITCH, the world's oldest original working digital computer from 1951, being restarted at The National Museum of Computing in 2012.
vVgc8ksstyg.why: Shared as a quick look at a vintage relay and dekatron computer running, along with praise for the museum.

ve4q-1D_Ajo.summary: A JRE clip in which Bret Weinstein explains his concern that most American lab mice descend from a single lab lineage. He argues this undermines how well mouse research translates to humans.
ve4q-1D_Ajo.why: HN links it when discussing mouse-study reliability and reproducibility.

vvr9AMWEU-c.summary: A spectrogram visualization of the sounds in a dial-up modem handshake, with an annotated image explaining each noise. It shows how the handshake's tones map to the negotiation steps.
vvr9AMWEU-c.why: Linked as a nostalgic and clear way to see what the modem handshake is doing, and as an example of sounds people can recognize.

vw9zyxm860Q.summary: Internet Historian's comedic retelling of how internet users located and captured the flag from Shia LaBeouf's He Will Not Divide Us installation, framed with Metal Gear Solid parodies. It covers the trolling campaign and the geolocation of the flag.
vw9zyxm860Q.why: HN refers to it as a humorous account of how online communities pinpointed the flag's location, used as an example of crowd-sourced geolocation.

vxWjtpzCIfA.summary: Not Just Bikes examines Toronto's GO Transit commuter rail, arguing it is a costly system with park-and-ride stations and rush-hour-only service that subsidizes car-dependent suburbs.
vxWjtpzCIfA.why: Cited in transit debates to show the cost and low utilization of commuter rail and the case for dense housing around stations.

vyEWLhOfLgQ.summary: PBS Space Time examines the Silurian hypothesis, the idea that an industrial civilization could have existed on Earth before humans. It looks at what traces such a civilization might leave in the geological record.
vyEWLhOfLgQ.why: HN uses it as an approachable treatment of whether an earlier industrial civilization would be detectable in geology.

vzGPq9LSjEw.summary: Tony Heller argues that US thermometer data shows a century of cooling and that NOAA adjusts the record to produce a warming trend.
vzGPq9LSjEw.why: Cited by commenters skeptical of climate data adjustments, to support claims about NOAA modeled data. The claims are contested.

vzZy1Aqleno.summary: A step-by-step guide to building a lifter, a small triangular ionocraft made from balsa wood, aluminum foil and thin wire, powered by a high-voltage supply. It also shows high-voltage safety practices.
vzZy1Aqleno.why: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of how lifters and ion wind propulsion work, mostly in threads about exotic propulsion and flying saucers.

v-n1vGeVIXo.summary: A short pronunciation clip showing how to say the word 'synecdoche'. It has almost no other content.
v-n1vGeVIXo.why: Cited only as a running joke, usually when someone brings up the word or the Charlie Kaufman film title.

v4boTbv9_nU.summary: Chris Pirillo has his father try Windows 8 for the first time to see how ordinary users cope with the new interface.
v4boTbv9_nU.why: Cited critically, as evidence that Windows 8 would frustrate ordinary users, especially without a start button.

v5GPWJPLcHg.summary: Cody's Lab collects a sample of dust from the side of a highway and refines it to recover platinum-group metals deposited by catalytic converters. The video walks through the chemistry of separating and assaying the precious metals.
v5GPWJPLcHg.why: HN commenters cite it as a vivid demonstration that roadside and tire/pavement dust contains recoverable platinum.

vAEU-Lf60LA.summary: A one-minute clip from Back to the Future Part II showing the Cafe 80's scene with Max Headroom-style pseudo-CGI waiters of Reagan, Michael Jackson, and Khomeini.
vAEU-Lf60LA.why: Cited in Max Headroom threads as an example of the show's visual style being copied in film.

vEOmzjImsVc.summary: A three-minute demo of ProFORMA, a system from Cambridge that builds textured 3D models live from a video of an object.
vEOmzjImsVc.why: HN cites it as an early demo of generating 3D models just by filming an object, in threads on Kinect, 3D printing and depth cameras.

vJpEuMidcSU.summary: A parody video contrasting Nokia's polished N97 promotional material with the sluggish, buggy reality of using the phone.
vJpEuMidcSU.why: Cited as an infamous example of the gap between marketing renders and shipped products.

vL-KQij0I8I.summary: A two-minute clip from The Devil Wears Prada in which Miranda Priestly explains how the cerulean color of a casual sweater traces back through runway designers to the bargain bin. It is a monologue about how high fashion trickles down to mass-market clothing.
vL-KQij0I8I.why: HN commenters cite it as shorthand for how trends and taste trickle down, and sometimes post it as a reflexive joke.

vL_syp1ZScM.summary: NFPA video in which wildfire researcher Jack Cohen explains that embers (firebrands), not the flame front, are the main cause of homes igniting in wildfires. He shows how landscaping and removing debris around the home reduce risk.
vL_syp1ZScM.why: HN commenters cite it as a source for the research showing that simple home-ignition-zone measures raise a house's chance of surviving a wildfire.

vLfghLQE3F4.summary: A short Fry and Laurie sketch in which a man returns from vacation to find his local police station has been privatized, with paid tiers of service. It satirizes privatization of public services.
vLfghLQE3F4.why: HN commenters use it as a joking reference when discussing privatization, outsourcing and absurd bureaucracy.

vMITcQUe-9M.summary: A one-minute clip from the Seinfeld episode 'The Shower Head'. It is a short sitcom scene about a low-flow shower head.
vMITcQUe-9M.why: Posted as a joke in threads about showers and product restrictions.

vQ5MA685ApE.summary: A short video of five people carrying a live, running web server across the city by public transport to a new datacenter. It stayed powered and connected to the internet the whole way, so there was no downtime.
vQ5MA685ApE.why: HN treats it as the classic example of moving a live server with zero downtime, brought up whenever the topic of uninterrupted migration comes up.

vUgs2O7Okqc.summary: A movie clip from Terry Gilliam's Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas in which Duke recalls the brief magical moment of 1960s San Francisco, the 'high water mark' monologue.
vUgs2O7Okqc.why: Quoted to describe fleeting cultural moments that cannot be repeated, such as early tech eras or SimCity 2000.

vXzuFprlyrw.summary: MKBHD drives a Tesla, a Mustang Mach-E and a gas car on a 1000-mile loop to compare total trip time and charging experience.
vXzuFprlyrw.why: HN cites it as real-world evidence on EV road trip times and the unreliability of non-Tesla charging networks.

vZw35VUBdzo.summary: The classic Monty Python sketch in which a customer tries to return a dead parrot to a pet shop owner who insists it is only resting.
vZw35VUBdzo.why: Used as a joke reference for denying that something obviously defunct is dead.

va1rzP2xIx4.summary: Technology Connections complains about the harsh, overly blue color of modern LED Christmas lights and tries more fixes for them. It follows earlier videos by the same creator on holiday lighting.
va1rzP2xIx4.why: HN cites it whenever LED holiday lights look wrong or give people headaches, as an explanation of why they seem too blue.

vbnySBqioB0.summary: A short clip of a Garry Kasparov press conference interrupted by a flying object in a prank. It is a brief, crude stunt video.
vbnySBqioB0.why: HN commenters cite it only as an early example of a politically motivated drone-style attack on Kasparov.

vc7WqVMCABg.summary: Thunderf00t argues that Zero Mass Water's solar-powered atmospheric water generator is essentially a dehumidifier with solar panels. He critiques its economics and physics, especially in arid places.
vc7WqVMCABg.why: Cited in threads on atmospheric water harvesting as the standard debunking of such startups.

vf-k6qOfXz0.summary: A short clip of Bernie Sanders in conversation with Ezra Klein of Vox, where he rejects open borders as a proposal that serves the Koch brothers. It is an excerpt from a longer interview on global poverty.
vf-k6qOfXz0.why: HN commenters cite it in immigration debates as evidence of Sanders' 2015 position that open borders and high immigration hurt wages.

vidzkYnaf6Y.summary: A very short clip from Yes, Prime Minister in which Sir Arnold and Sir Humphrey run through a piece of circular political reasoning. It is the origin of the so-called politician's logic.
vidzkYnaf6Y.why: HN uses it as a joke reference to the politician's fallacy, to mock reasoning of the form 'something must be done, this is something, so do it'.

vijGdWn5-h8.summary: National Geographic footage showing the cordyceps fungus infecting ants and other insects and steering their behavior so it can reproduce.
vijGdWn5-h8.why: Cited as a vivid example of parasites controlling host behavior whenever zombie-fungus comparisons come up.

vix6TMnj9vY.summary: A 1979 BBC Tomorrow's World segment where Michael Rodd tries an experimental British cordless mobile phone prototype.
vix6TMnj9vY.why: Shared as a period piece showing how past TV predicted technologies that later became common.

vjqt8T3tJIE.summary: Vsauce explores whether people in past decades really looked older than people of the same age today, or whether photographic and cultural factors make them seem so. It draws on old photos, yearbooks and perception research.
vjqt8T3tJIE.why: HN commenters cite it to explain why people in old photos seem older than they were.

vqeIeIcDHD0.summary: Physics Girl creator Dianna Cowern shares an update on her health, struggling with long COVID and ME/CFS. It includes documentary footage and links for supporting her recovery.
vqeIeIcDHD0.why: Shared in threads on chronic fatigue and her return as an update on how she is doing.

vt9kRLrmrjc.summary: A short CNN news segment reporting that the FBI is looking at a phone call between Tamerlan Tsarnaev's widow and her husband after his photos were released. It is brief 2013 coverage of the Boston bombing investigation.
vt9kRLrmrjc.why: HN commenters cite it as an example of claims that government can access digital communications and that none is secure.

vydgkCCXbTA.summary: A health update from the Physics Girl channel explaining that Dianna Cowern has been seriously ill with long COVID and ME/CFS, and that new science videos are postponed.
vydgkCCXbTA.why: HN uses it as an example of how severe long COVID and ME/CFS can become.

vzm6pvHPSGo.summary: A 2000 IBM commercial in which Avery Brooks complains that we still have no flying cars. It plays on the failed futurist promises of the twentieth century.
vzm6pvHPSGo.why: HN commenters reference it, sometimes jokingly, in flying-car threads as an ironic sign that culture had written off the idea.
